description:
FILED s473t6a (Opus, 2026-09-16) by #1501 ROUND 8 (t6a).  PRE-EXISTING.
THE BIGGEST SINGLE PRIZE THE ROUND FOUND: 93 blessed companion rows plus 50
rows perl produces that PCL never reaches.

perl lets an `@INC` element be a HOOK instead of a directory:
  * a CODE ref, called as `$hook->($hook, $filename)`;
  * an ARRAY ref whose [0] is a code ref (or an object), called with the whole
    array ref as the invocant;
  * a blessed OBJECT with an `INC` method (or, since 5.38, `INCDIR`);
and the hook returns a list that may hold a filehandle, a ref to the source
TEXT, a filter code ref and a state scalar -- or nothing, which means "not
found, try the next @INC entry".  `%INC{$filename}` is then set to the HOOK
itself, not to a path.

PCL treats every @INC element as a pathname.  `%p-inc-dir-file`
(cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) does

    (s (if (stringp d) d (namestring d)))

so a non-string element reaches SBCL's `namestring` and the program gets a RAW
HOST ERROR, not a perl one:

    The value
      #<function (lambda (&rest %_args) :in "/tmp/â¦/prog.lisp") {B800D8AB5B}>
    is not of type
      (or string pathname synonym-stream file-stream)

which aborts the enclosing top-level form.  (`%p-transpile-inc-args` already
has the right instinct one function away: it SKIPS a non-string entry, with a
docstring saying a code ref or object hook "has no `-I` spelling".)

MEASURED ROWS (baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv, all now carrying this task):
  t/op/inccode.t        76 rows = the WHOLE file (13/26 produced, 50 of perl's
                        89 never produced behind four aborted forms).  Every
                        row is a hook: "require Foo; magic via code ref",
                        "val Foo.pm is a coderef in %INC", "magic via array
                        ref", "magic via scalar object", "require Quux3 via
                        AUTOLOADed INC", "FETCH is called once on scalar-tied
                        @INC elem", "INCDIR works as expected".
  t/op/require_errors.t 17 rows (its tests 57-73): "@INC hook blocks do not
                        cause segfault", "Inc hooks have the correct cop_file",
                        "INC hooks that overwrite @INC continue as expected",
                        "Objects with no INC or INCDIR method â¦ throw an
                        error", "Blessed subs with INCDIR methods call INCDIR",
                        "INCDIR ref returns are stringified".

RULE 12 FIRST, WHATEVER ELSE: a non-string @INC element is a MISSING CASE that
today leaks a host error.  The cheapest honest step is to make
`%p-inc-dir-file` announce once and SKIP (`%p-announce-unsupported`), so the
require then fails with perl's own "Can't locate Foo.pm in @INC" instead of an
SBCL type error -- it fixes no row by itself but turns 93 host-error rows into
perl-shaped ones and stops four forms aborting.  s473t6a did NOT take even that
step: the round's budget went to #1813, and a change to the require path wants
the full sweep behind it.

FIX SHAPE (the real one).  `p-find-module-in-inc` must classify each element
before probing it, and a hook needs a way to hand SOURCE TEXT to the loader --
PCL's require path works on FILES (`p-transpile-file` takes a path), so a hook
that returns a filehandle or `\$text` has to be spooled to a temp file (or the
transpile server given a string entry point).  That is a NEW MECHANISM, which
is why this is filed and not fixed.  PROBE THE BREAKING CASE: `@INC` normally
holds strings only, and `%p-inc-dir-file` is on the module-load hot path, so
the classification must cost one `stringp` on the common element.


=== QUEUED (s530, Fable, 2026-10-31) ===
One of the 41 REAL whole-file CPAN board failures (the USER-asked review; 138 FAIL files = 69 perl-skips + 4 fixed + 2 perl-fails + 22 ruled not-supported + 41 real).  Queued as s531a member 2 (5 files: Path-Tiny 2, URI 2, Log-Log4perl 1) -- `briefs-and-rules-for-claude-subagents/s530/s531a-prompt.md` / `s531b-prompt.md`.


=== DONE (s531a, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-01) ===
@INC hooks implemented in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp: %p-require-locate (require, require "x.pl"; an explicit path that does not open is offered to the hooks only) and %p-do-locate (do FILE) walk @INC calling a hook in its place (%p-inc-hook-run): a CODE ref with (element, NAME); an unblessed ARRAY ref through its [0] with the array as first argument; a blessed object through INC (an AUTOLOAD answers), else INCDIR (searched as directories), else a blessed CODE ref as code, else a ""-overloaded object as a directory, else perl's die; the answer items in perl's order (%p-inc-hook-source: initial-text ref, filehandle -- a lexical handle arrives as its stream --, generator / filter sub over $_ with run_user_filter's status rule, state); the text is spooled to a private temp file (%p-inc-hook-spool) and loaded uncached; %INC = the hook element unless the hook stored an entry.  p-find-module-in-inc (the directory resolver: cache dependency check, no-load pragmas, PPI's sources) SKIPS hooks; an undef element is skipped and a number is its string (%p-inc-dir-file; it was a raw SBCL type error).  Probes scratch/s531a/pr/inc1.pl inc2.pl: every behaviour = perl (message text aside).  Guard Pl/t/inc-hook-01.t (2 rows, both FAIL on ade297e7).  ir-spec 9.0b.  Board: URI scheme-exceptions 6/0 + urn-scheme-exceptions 6/0, Log4perl 053Resurrect 1/0 (3 *FILE* rows out); Path-Tiny input_output_no_PU_UU / no_UU run to input_output.t's own #660 face (re-caused).  NOT done: a TIED @INC element's FETCH-once rows (inccode.t) and the hook source's __FILE__ (#4161).  Companion op/inccode.t + op/require_errors.t: see the s531a report.  Branch head: b969a960.
